claims.text: CALPHAD-based high-throughput computing can rapidly screen large multicomponent HEA composition spaces for stable phases.
CALPHAD can provide initial melting-point estimates for refractory high-entropy alloys.
Moment Tensor Potentials can be trained on DFT data from elemental, binary, ternary, and quaternary subsystems of Nb-Ta-Mo-W.
For MoNbTaW, an MTP can reproduce DFT energies and forces with low errors and capture variations associated with local chemical environments.
Random-solid-solution and equilibrium short-range-ordered states can be constructed for single-phase MoNbTaW using hybrid molecular-dynamics/Monte-Carlo simulations.
Molecular dynamics with MLIPs can compute heat capacity, entropy of fusion, and melting temperature through two-phase coexistence or free-energy methods for RHEAs.
Chemical short-range order and local lattice distortions modulate phonon spectra and anharmonic vibrational contributions to RHEA thermodynamic properties.
MLIPs capture nonlinear many-body interactions and SRO-induced variations in vibrational entropy and anharmonicity.
Capturing SRO-induced vibrational entropy and anharmonicity enables accurate prediction of RHEA melting properties.
Standard empirical potentials such as EAM and MEAM fail to capture SRO and many-body effects in multicomponent RHEAs.
The deficiencies of standard empirical potentials cause large errors in predicted melting properties.
Pure DFT is computationally prohibitive for screening vast RHEA composition spaces.
CALPHAD provides a thermodynamically consistent phase-stability baseline based on Gibbs-energy minimization.
CALPHAD screening reduces the composition search space needed for subsequent MLIP training and validation.
The hybrid framework can predict RHEA melting temperatures within plus or minus 50 K.
The hybrid framework can accurately predict entropy of fusion and heat capacity across vast RHEA composition spaces.
The hybrid framework has computational cost orders of magnitude lower than pure DFT.
The hybrid framework is more accurate for melting properties than empirical potentials.
The method is valid for single-phase BCC or FCC solid solutions in which SRO is the dominant microstructural feature.
Systems with intermetallic precipitation, phase separation, or extreme nonequilibrium states require explicit phase-field coupling and lie outside the method's validity.
